motion: Did Jesus rise from the dead, and can historical evidence plus allegedly supernatural phenomena justify that conclusion?

burdens.description: Establish that empirical reports provide affirmative evidence for a supernatural dimension of reality.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify observable reported events with external corroboration, explain which ordinary alternatives that corroboration excludes, and state the resulting evidential implication for a supernatural dimension.

burdens.description: Establish that Jesus's resurrection is the best explanation of the relevant historical evidence.
burdens.successCriteria: Substantiate the claimed appearance data and compare the resurrection with live alternatives using explanatory scope, explanatory power, ad hocness, and compatibility with established background knowledge.

burdens.description: Show that the pro case has not justified moving from unexplained reports to a supernatural cause.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify the missing test or causal bridge, show that the cited observations do not distinguish a supernatural cause from live error, fraud, hallucination, or unknown-natural alternatives, and state why suspension remains warranted.

burdens.description: Show that the surviving historical evidence is insufficient to warrant the resurrection conclusion.
burdens.successCriteria: Identify a material source or attestation limitation, or an unsupported possibility assumption, and explain how it prevents the resurrection from being established over live non-resurrection alternatives.

source.limitations: The source is a locally normalized human English YouTube-caption track with no speaker labels and with occasional name, grammar, and word-segmentation errors. Selected speakers are high-confidence from the announced formal turn structure and unambiguous question-and-answer handoffs. No local audio-verification asset was supplied, so no medium- or low-confidence candidate was eligible; all excerpts preserve caption wording exactly. Partial caption-event boundaries are time-proportioned to isolate one speaker's atomic act.

inventoryProtocol.selectionStatement: The inventory takes each side's first two load-bearing constructive acts from the openings, then samples the earliest qualifying responsive atomic acts two at a time from successive quarters of the formal rebuttal-and-cross-examination exchange (00:58:01.440 through 01:44:45), carrying exclusions forward. The resulting 12 moves are chronological, include 5 con and 7 pro acts without imposed symmetry, and leave moderator and audience logistics outside the responsive sampling frame.
